prediction.likelyOutcome: The lender is very likely to prevail on guaranty liability given the clean bankruptcy-triggered recourse provision and the strongly pro-lender findings from the prior Washtenaw litigation and bankruptcy proceedings (borrower mismanagement, affirmed foreclosure, affirmed receiver appointment). The size of the ultimate deficiency judgment turns on an unresolved credit-bid-allocation dispute this record doesn't fully quantify, and Schubiner's DACA and lien-based counterclaims face serious collateral-estoppel problems from the earlier Packard Square litigation, meaning any offset is likely to be modest relative to the total exposure.

outcome.description: On cross-motions, the trial court granted summary disposition to the lender on its guaranty claim and on Schubiner's counterclaims and on December 17, 2019 entered judgment against him for $13,992,936.05 (the original-loan balance left after the lender applied its $75 million credit bid first to the receiver loan), plus attorney fees, consultant fees, continuing interest and costs. The Court of Appeals affirmed the judgment (Docket No. 352510), while vacating a separate postjudgment order on intervenors' properties.
